title: 18 Vibe Coding Prompts to Copy and Customize for Apps in 2026
summary: Copy 18 vibe coding prompts for business apps, customize their data and workflows, and check permissions, calculations, and saved changes before launch.
body_markdown:
Useful **vibe coding prompts** specify a business task, its data, who may act, and how to check the result—not just what the screen should look like.


Below are 18 copyable prompts for client portals, CRMs, approvals, dashboards, and operations tools. Each includes fields to customize and a practical acceptance check.


**These are illustrative requirements, not tested implementations.** Example fields, formulas, thresholds, and statuses are editorial choices. Requested behavior is not evidence of platform support or a verified implementation.


> **Key Takeaways** Specify users, source data, fields, permitted actions, constraints, and acceptance criteria.Combine each example with the shared setup block, using synthetic or approved test data.Check stored records, calculations, workflows, and access—not just appearance.Request focused repairs, rerun tests, and treat publishing as a separate decision.


**Jump to:**


- Customize the prompts
- Client and agency apps: 1–3
- CRM and real estate: 4–6
- Approvals and professional services: 7–9
- Marketing and analytics: 10–12
- Property and service operations: 13–15
- Small-business data management: 16–18
- Validation, repairs, and worksheet


## How to Customize These Vibe Coding Prompts


Choose one workflow, replace the placeholders, and define success before generating the app. “Assign intake requests” is a clearer starting point than “manage our agency.”


Use this reusable **vibe coding prompt template** :


**Business task → users and roles → source data → fields and relationships → permitted actions → interface → constraints → acceptance checks**


### Shared setup block


**Every numbered example depends on this block. Copy it together with your chosen prompt and its acceptance check.** Resolve placeholders such as` \[data source\]` ,` \[role\]` ,` \[status labels\]` , and` \[date range\]` before building.


```text
Build for [business/team] using [data source] in an approved test
environment. Use synthetic or approved test records only.


Inspect the available schema and propose field mappings first.
Ask about missing fields, relationships, integrations, or unclear
rules instead of inventing them.


Enforce the specified read and write permissions at the data/action
layer, not only by hiding controls. Deny access not explicitly
granted. Ask me to resolve any incomplete role or record scope.


Persist approved changes to the intended source. Show loading,
empty, validation, and failure states without false success.


Do not change the source schema or enable external messages,
payments, or destructive actions without approval.
Identify unsupported requirements and manual configuration needed.
Treat the appended acceptance checks as tests to run, not results.


```


Jet Admin’s[AI Internal Tool Builder](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/ai-internal-tool-builder?ref=jetadmin.io) page describes generating tools on existing business data and manually editing them when prompting falls short. Generation, configuration, and validation remain separate steps.


Configure credentials through approved connection settings; never paste them into prompts. Confirm that your organization permits both the builder and the data you plan to use.


## Client and Agency App Prompts


Client-facing apps need explicit record and file boundaries. Copy each example with the shared setup block above.


### 1. Client Project Portal


Give clients project visibility without exposing other accounts. Jet Admin’s[Client Portal](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/client-portal?ref=jetadmin.io) describes branded spaces for projects, file sharing, and team messaging—not a tested implementation of this prompt.


```text
With the shared setup block, create a client project portal.
Relate clients, projects, deliverables, files, and updates by stable IDs.


Project fields: title, client ID, owner, due date, and status.
Statuses: Planned, Active, Awaiting Client, Finished.


Clients may view their own projects, download approved shared files,
upload to their projects, and comment. Admins manage all projects,
statuses, and file visibility. Internal notes remain admin-only.


Use [brand colors] and a compact project summary. Enforce client
isolation for records, uploads, downloads, and direct file links.


```


**Customize:** Client identity mapping, status labels, storage, and branding.
**Why it matters:** Project access and file access need separate checks.
**Acceptance check:** With two client accounts, attempt to open each other’s project and file URLs. Both cross-client attempts must fail.


### 2. Client Intake and Assignment App


Turn incoming requests into owned work with a reliable confirmation.


```text
With the shared setup block, build an intake app. Require contact
name, valid email, organization, project type, description, and
consent to [approved data-use notice].


Allowed project types: Brand Strategy, Website, Content.
Assign each type using [assignment mapping]; route an allowed type
without an available assignee to the Unassigned queue.


Submitters may create requests but cannot browse intake records.
Intake Coordinators may view requests and update owner and status.
Store consent timestamp and notice version; keep optional marketing
consent separate.


Show a reference number only after saving succeeds. Confirm
[approved response window] without sending external messages.


```


**Customize:** Project types, assignment mapping, consent wording, and response window.
**Why it matters:** Confirmation should reflect a saved record, not a button click.
**Acceptance check:** Submit an invalid email and an unsupported project type, then a valid request. Only the valid request should persist in the intended source with the correct assignment.


### 3. Deliverable Review Tracker


Keep feedback and approval attached to the exact version reviewed.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a deliverable review tracker.
Store project ID, title, owner, due date, and assigned reviewers.
Owners and assigned reviewers may access the deliverable.


Store each version separately: version ID, number, file reference,
uploader, timestamp, and status. Statuses: Draft, In Review,
Changes Requested, Approved.


Owners submit Draft versions for review. Only assigned reviewers
may decide on In Review versions. Any change request moves the
version to Changes Requested; approval requires every assigned
reviewer to approve that version. Freeze reviewer assignments
during review.


Attach feedback and decisions to version IDs. New versions start
as Draft and inherit neither feedback links nor approvals.


```


**Customize:** Reviewer assignments, approval policy, and due-date rules.
**Why it matters:** Replacing a file must not transfer approval to new content.
**Acceptance checks:** Feedback on version one must remain there after version two is uploaded. With two reviewers, one approval must not approve the version; version two must begin without either approval.


## CRM and Real Estate Prompts


Define the pipeline and ownership model before requesting a board. Jet Admin’s[Build Custom CRM](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/crm?ref=jetadmin.io) describes adapting a CRM to a team’s fields, pipeline, and database.


### 4. Sales Pipeline CRM


Make visibility, stage names, and reporting definitions match your sales process.


```text
With the shared setup block, create a CRM. Require deal name,
company ID, owner ID, amount, currency, expected close date,
and stage.


Stages: Unqualified, Qualified, Proposal, Decision, Closed Won,
Closed Lost. Require closed date for closed deals.


Reps may view and edit only assigned deals. Managers may view and
edit deals belonging to their mapped team, not other teams.
Apply this scope to related company data and reports.


Provide a stage board and table sorted by expected close date
ascending, then deal ID. Win rate for [date range] equals
Closed Won count divided by Closed Won plus Closed Lost count,
using closed date. Show N/A when no closed deals qualify.


```


**Customize:** Stages, team mapping, date range, and currency policy.
**Why it matters:** Restricting editing does not establish who may view deals.
**Acceptance checks:** Save a stage change and reload; it must persist with no unrequested stages. A rep must also fail to open another rep’s deal directly.


### 5. Lead Follow-Up Queue


Use one timestamp rule for both eligibility and sorting.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a follow-up queue using lead ID,
owner ID, created timestamp, last-contact timestamp, stage,
and next-action note.


Effective contact timestamp equals last-contact timestamp when
present, otherwise created timestamp. Include open leads when
elapsed time since that timestamp is at least [threshold hours].
Exclude Closed Won and Closed Lost.


Calculate elapsed time in UTC; display in [timezone]. Sort by
effective contact timestamp ascending, then lead ID. Flag missing
created and contact timestamps as data errors, not eligible leads.


Reps may view and update assigned leads; managers may view and
update their team's leads. Log Contact persists the contact
timestamp before showing success.


```


**Customize:** Threshold, excluded stages, timezone, and qualifying contact actions.
**Why it matters:** Never-contacted leads need a defined place in the queue.
**Acceptance check:** At a fixed test time, test contacted and never-contacted leads below, exactly at, and above the threshold. Verify eligibility and oldest-effective-timestamp ordering.


### 6. Property Showing Scheduler


Specify conflict handling independently of the calendar’s appearance.


```text
With the shared setup block, create a mobile showing scheduler.
Appointments link property ID, client ID, agent ID, start time,
duration, and status: Scheduled, Completed, Cancelled.


Agents may view and manage their appointments and associated clients.
Scheduling Coordinators may manage the team's appointments.
Clients have no app access in this version.


Display [timezone]; store unambiguous timestamps. Require
[buffer minutes] between an agent's appointments. Block overlapping
Scheduled appointments for the same agent or property; cancelled
appointments reserve no time.


Provide day/week views and large controls. Enforce conflicts on
save and reschedule, including simultaneous bookings. No reminders.


```


**Customize:** Duration, buffer, timezone, and scheduling roles.
**Why it matters:** Two users can both see availability before either saves.
**Acceptance checks:** Reject an overlapping booking without changing the existing one. Submit conflicting appointments simultaneously from two sessions; at most one may persist.


## Approval and Professional-Service Workflow Prompts


Approval apps need rules for who can act and what happens next. Jet Admin’s[Approval Workflow](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/approval-workflow?ref=jetadmin.io) describes multistep routing with an auditable trail. The policies below remain proposed requirements.


### 7. Purchase Request Approval App


Define routing, self-approval restrictions, and the exact authority of each reviewer.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a purchase approval app.
Fields: requester, department, supplier, description, amount,
currency, status. Require a positive amount in [single currency].


Requesters view their own requests and edit Drafts. Assigned managers
and finance reviewers view requests routed to them.
Draft moves to Manager Review on submission. Manager approval sends
amounts above [threshold] to Finance Review; other amounts become
Approved. Only assigned finance reviewers may approve Finance Review.


No self-approval; ask for an alternate approver where roles overlap.
Either assigned reviewer may reject at their step with a reason.
Rejected returns to Draft through requester revision only.


Freeze submitted amounts. Record actor, timestamp, old/new status,
and decision reason for every transition.


```


**Customize:** Threshold, approver mapping, currency, and alternate approvers.
**Why it matters:** A status label does not itself enforce an approval boundary.
**Acceptance check:** On a request awaiting Finance Review, have its requester and manager attempt final approval. Both must fail; the assigned, non-requester finance reviewer must be able to approve.


### 8. Expense Review Queue


Define reviewer scope and employee visibility alongside retry handling.


```text
With the shared setup block, create an expense queue. Require
employee, expense date, category, positive amount, currency,
and receipt.


Employees may view only their own expenses and history, and edit
only their Draft or Returned claims. Reviewers may view expenses
only for [assigned departments]; no self-review.


Statuses: Draft, Submitted, Returned, Approved. Employees submit
Draft or Returned claims. Assigned reviewers may approve Submitted
claims or return them with a reason, but cannot change amounts.


Resubmission keeps the expense ID and creates a new revision.
Repeated submission clicks or network retries must create only
one submission event per revision. Keep decision history.
Do not initiate reimbursement.


```


**Customize:** Categories, receipt rules, department mapping, and reviewer assignments.
**Why it matters:** Duplicate prevention and review authority are separate controls.
**Acceptance checks:** Double-submit and retry one revision; expect one expense and one submission event. An unrelated employee or out-of-scope reviewer must not read or approve it.


### 9. Legal or Tax Document Intake Tracker


Track document collection without automating professional judgment.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a document intake tracker.
Relate matters, clients, required document categories, files,
responsible staff, and manually entered deadlines.


Categories: Identity, Engagement, Supporting Records, Other.
Statuses: Requested, Received, Needs Replacement, Accepted.
Flag missing required categories and overdue supplied deadlines.


Assigned staff and authorized supervisors may view and manage
their matters and files. Other staff have no access.
If client uploads are enabled, clients may view their own request
list and upload to their own matters, but not read internal notes.


Do not calculate statutory deadlines, interpret documents,
or provide legal or tax advice.


```


**Customize:** Categories, staff assignments, client access, and supplied deadlines.
**Why it matters:** Administrative tracking should remain separate from legal or tax advice.
**Acceptance check:** Create a missing-document condition. Assigned staff should see the flag; an unrelated user must not see the matter or files.


## Marketing and Analytics Prompts


Specify metric definitions, source records, and filters before chart types. Jet Admin’s[Analytics Dashboard](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/analytics-dashboard?ref=jetadmin.io) describes warehouse-backed analysis with filtering and record drill-down.


### 10. Campaign Performance Dashboard


Define the reporting grain and preserve records without matching conversions.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a read-only campaign dashboard
using [spend source] and [conversion source].


Aggregate each source to campaign ID plus reporting date in
[timezone] before joining. Use a full outer join on both keys,
retaining spend-only and conversion-only rows. Treat an absent
matching aggregate as zero, but flag invalid source values.


Use [date range], [reporting currency], and the source's
[attribution model]; do not infer attribution.


Show total spend, conversions, and cost per conversion:
sum(spend) / sum(conversions). Show N/A for zero conversions.
Provide campaign filters, source drill-down, and last refresh time.
Apply [role-to-campaign mapping] to summaries and detail records.


```


**Customize:** Source mappings, attribution, dates, currency, and access scope.
**Why it matters:** Pre-aggregation prevents multiplication; join choice determines which campaigns survive.
**Acceptance check:** Reconcile a small dataset containing matched, spend-only, and conversion-only campaigns. Spend-only campaigns must retain their spend and show zero conversions with N/A cost per conversion.


### 11. Revenue and Sales Dashboard


Define both the metric and how multi-product transactions are allocated.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a read-only sales dashboard.
Define Net Collected Sales as settled payments minus completed
refunds, using each event's settlement timestamp in [date range].
Exclude pending/failed events and report currencies separately.


Use stable transaction IDs. Map payments and refunds to products
through [approved transaction-to-line-item allocation source].
Require allocated amounts to equal each transaction total.
If allocations are missing, flag them and use an Unallocated bucket;
never repeat a full order amount for every product.


Group by day in [timezone], allocated product, and recorded order
owner. Apply [role-to-record scope] to summaries and details.
Label this operational metric, not accounting revenue recognition.


```


**Customize:** Settlement fields, allocation source, owner mapping, and refund treatment.
**Why it matters:** Product grouping can duplicate order-level totals without explicit allocation.
**Acceptance check:** Reconcile one currency containing a multi-product payment and partial refund. Product allocations, including Unallocated, must sum to the same net total as transaction details.


### 12. Event Check-In App


Use stable identifiers so repeated actions do not inflate attendance.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a mobile event check-in app.
Authorize staff only for events in [staff-to-event mapping].
Identify attendance by event ID plus attendee ID.


Search by name/email or scan a QR code with an opaque attendee
reference. Require staff authentication; a QR code alone grants
no record access.


Record first check-in timestamp and staff ID. Repeated attempts
show Already Checked In and preserve the first timestamp.
Enforce one attendance record per event-attendee pair, including
simultaneous scans. Count unique checked-in attendees per event.


```


**Customize:** Search fields, QR format, and staff event assignments.
**Why it matters:** Duplicate handling must work across devices.
**Acceptance check:** Check in the same attendee simultaneously from two devices. Attendance must increase by one, with one stored check-in record.


## Property, Contractor, and Service Operations Prompts


Field tools need ownership rules and usable mobile states. A responsive interface does not establish offline support.


### 13. Maintenance Request Tracker


Separate requester, contractor, and manager access.


```text
With the shared setup block, create a maintenance tracker.
Fields: property ID, unit ID, requester ID, description, priority,
assignee, created timestamp, status.


Priorities: Urgent for active damage, High for loss of essential
service, Routine otherwise. Statuses: New, Assigned, In Progress,
Waiting, Resolved.


Requesters create and view only their own requests at permitted
properties. Managers manage requests at assigned properties.
Contractors see assigned jobs and update progress, not assignments.
Internal notes are manager-only.


Provide a mobile form and [approved emergency contact instructions].
State that this is not an emergency reporting channel.


```


**Customize:** Priority definitions, property mapping, and emergency instructions.
**Why it matters:** Property membership need not expose every resident’s requests.
**Acceptance check:** Test users at different properties and two requesters at one property. Direct access to unpermitted requests must fail.


### 14. Contractor Job Schedule


Treat reassignment as a new availability check.


```text
With the shared setup block, build a contractor schedule.
Store job ID, location, required skills, worker IDs, start time,
duration, status, availability, and approved leave.


Schedulers manage jobs in [team scope]; workers view only their
assigned jobs. In [timezone], block assignments outside availability
or overlapping another active job. Require [travel buffer minutes]
between jobs. Cancelled jobs reserve no time.


Provide day/week views. Reassignment must validate the replacement
worker's skills, leave, and availability before saving.
Preserve the previous assignment on failure. Do not infer travel
time from addresses without an approved integration.


```


**Customize:** Team scope, skills, travel buffer, and working hours.
**Why it matters:** A valid original assignment does not make its replacement valid.
**Acceptance check:** Try overlapping assignments and reassignment to an unavailable worker. Reject both conflicts and preserve the original schedule.


### 15. Support Ticket Queue


Define access, transitions, and response timing separately.


```text
With the shared setup block, create a queue using [ticket source].
Fields: ticket ID, customer ID, subject, team ID, owner, created time,
first human response time, priority, status.


Agents view/update assigned tickets only. Team Leads view/manage
their team's tickets and reassign within that team. No customer
login or cross-team access in this version.


Transitions: New to Assigned; Assigned to Waiting for Customer
or Resolved; Waiting for Customer to Assigned or Resolved;
Resolved to Closed or Assigned; Closed to Assigned by Team Leads only.


Priority: Critical for unavailable service, High for blocked work,
Normal otherwise. First-response deadline is creation time plus
[response hours by priority], in UTC. Ownership changes never
reset it; only a recorded human response clears its flag.
Exclude Resolved/Closed from active queues. Log status/owner changes.


```


**Customize:** Team mapping, priorities, response targets, and transitions.
**Why it matters:** Reassignment should neither expand access accidentally nor erase deadlines.
**Acceptance check:** Reassign one ticket and close another. Verify scoped ownership counts, unchanged deadlines, closed-ticket exclusion, and loss of access for the former assignee.


## Small-Business Data Management Prompts


Define permitted writes before designing forms. Atomicity, concurrency control, and retry safety below are requirements to verify—not guaranteed builder capabilities.


### 16. Inventory Adjustment App


Make inventory changes traceable and safe under retries.


```text
With the shared setup block, build an inventory adjustment app.
Identify stock by item ID plus location ID. Require integer adjustment
quantity, reason, operator, and unique operation ID.
Reasons: Count Correction, Damage, Return.


Inventory Managers may adjust stock at assigned locations;
other authorized location staff have read-only access.
Reject zero quantities and adjustments producing negative stock.
Do not allow direct editing of calculated stock.


Apply each operation ID once. Check current stock and save the
adjustment atomically, including concurrent requests.
Record before/after quantities, actor, reason, and timestamp.


```


**Customize:** Quantity units, location scope, reasons, and authorized roles.
**Why it matters:** Valid-looking forms cannot establish safe concurrent writes.
**Acceptance checks:** A below-zero adjustment must change nothing. Retrying one operation ID must apply it once. With stock of five, two simultaneous adjustments of minus four must not both succeed.


### 17. Invoice Follow-Up Tracker


Separate drafting, approval, and permission to send.


```text
With the shared setup block, build an invoice follow-up tracker.
Fields: invoice ID, customer ID, due date, currency, invoice amount,
applied payments, applied credits, payment status.


Outstanding balance equals amount minus payments and credits.
Queue overdue invoices only with positive balances; exclude Void.
Use [timezone] for due-date boundaries.


Billing Staff view assigned accounts and draft reminders.
Finance Approvers view/approve within [account scope].
Sending stays disabled until [approved integration] is authorized.


Bind approval to the exact message and invoice; edits invalidate it.
Recheck balance before sending and prevent duplicate sends.


```


**Customize:** Balance fields, account scope, timezone, and delivery integration.
**Why it matters:** Payment may arrive between drafting and sending.
**Acceptance check:** An unapproved reminder must not send. After approval, fully pay its invoice; it must leave the queue and remain unsendable despite the earlier approval.


### 18. Controlled Database Editing App


Use an editable-field allowlist instead of general table access.


```text
With the shared setup block, create an editor for [table].
Search by record ID, organization name, and contact email.
Read-only: record ID, tenant ID, created timestamp.
Editable: contact email, owner ID, account status.


Apply [role-to-record mapping] to reads. Only Data Stewards may
edit records in their assigned scope. Validate email format,
owner existence within the permitted tenant, and [status labels].


Bulk edits require explicit record selection, [maximum batch size],
affected-count preview, and confirmation. Apply identical field,
access, and value validation to single and bulk edits.
Report failures per record. Record actor, timestamp, record ID,
and before/after values for successful changes.


```


**Customize:** Table, record scope, field allowlist, status labels, and batch limit.
**Why it matters:** A filter should not silently authorize changes to every matching record.
**Acceptance check:** Attempt unauthorized and invalid writes, then an approved two-record update. Only the intended valid changes may persist; inspect unselected records too.


## Checks Before Using a Generated Business App


A successful preview is not a release decision. Check behavior in underlying records and authorization controls before inviting broader use.


Jet Admin’s[SQL Database Editor](https://www.jetadmin.io/use-cases/sql-data-editor?ref=jetadmin.io) describes search, filtering, bulk editing, per-field permissions, write validation, and an audit log. Those capabilities identify useful inspection areas; they do not prove that a particular generated configuration is correct.


Area What to verify


Source connection Reads and writes use the intended environment, source, and table.


Persistence Saved changes survive reload and appear in the source.


Calculations Known inputs reconcile, including zero, empty, and boundary cases.


Access Each role has only its specified record, field, file, and action permissions.


Workflow Unauthorized transitions, self-approval, and skipped steps fail.


Failure handling Connection errors show no false success or unexplained partial changes.


Repeated actions Retries and concurrent requests do not duplicate or corrupt records.


Change history Individual and bulk edits identify affected records, actors, and changes.


**Test beyond hidden controls.** In an authorized test environment, try direct record and file URLs with restricted accounts. Ask a technical collaborator to verify action/API-level authorization and concurrency controls where needed.


Inspect records after both successful and failed writes. If the platform cannot implement a required control, record an unresolved requirement rather than continuing to rephrase the prompt.


### Use a focused repair prompt


These AI app builder prompts work best when repairs name the discrepancy and preserve unrelated behavior:


```text
Observed behavior: [what happened].
Expected behavior: [the requirement].
Reproduction steps: [role, test records, actions, actual result].


Requested scope: inspect and change only [component, query,
permission, or transition]. Explain the cause before changing it.


Must remain unchanged: [schema, other permissions, navigation,
styling, and unrelated workflows].


Regression check: repeat [failing test] and [adjacent working test].
List unresolved limitations and manual steps. Report a test as
passed only if it was actually run and the result was observed.


```


For example, repair invoice balance and eligibility logic when paid invoices remain in a queue; do not request a rebuild of the entire app.


### Keep a prompt-and-test worksheet


Copy this CSV into a text file named` prompt-and-test-worksheet.csv` and open it in your spreadsheet tool. Add one row per requirement.


```text
Prompt,Requirement,Expected behavior,Observed behavior,Unresolved issue,Owner
1,Client isolation,Client A cannot open Client B files,Not tested,Run direct-link test,
4,Persistent writes,Saved stage survives reload,Not tested,Inspect source record,
10,Unmatched spend,Spend-only campaign retained with N/A cost per conversion,Not tested,Reconcile sample data,
16,Retry safety,Same operation ID changes stock once,Not tested,Run retry test,


```


Record the app version, environment, tester, and date alongside the worksheet. Keep “not tested” distinct from “passed.”


## Related Resources


The six Jet Admin pages linked in context above cover internal tools, client portals, custom CRMs, approvals, analytics, and controlled data editing. They describe application categories and product capabilities—not documented customer projects or measured outcomes. Confirm the implementation path and applicable plan before relying on a specific capability.


**Choose one prompt, adapt it to approved test data, and run its acceptance checks.** Fix observed failures, repeat the relevant tests, and make publishing a separate decision from approving the visual preview.
